grapes.style: Crisp, citrusy, mineral medium-bodied white; best young and unoaked; Vinho Verde versions spritzy and sharper.
Dry, perfumed, medium-bodied white with pear, almond, herbs and chalk; naturally low acid; drink young.
Bone-dry, sharp, lemony, volcanic-mineral white; also richer, oaked and Vinsanto dessert styles.
Barrel-aged sweet wine, at least half Assyrtiko; like tawny port crossed with late-harvest Riesling.

places: France (Loire: Vouvray, Savennières, Anjou, Saumur, Montlouis; Limoux)
grapes.style: High-acid apple-quince-chalk white made bone-dry, off-dry, sparkling or botrytized sweet.

places: Italy (Veneto: Soave Classico, Bianco di Custoza)
grapes.style: Citrus, white peach, ginger and almond white with racy acidity; sweet Recioto version tastes of honey and marmalade.
Peppery, citrus, green-bean and lentil-scented dry white; also off-dry and sweet Prädikat styles.

places: France (northern Rhône: Hermitage, St.-Joseph, Crozes-Hermitage, St.-Péray)
grapes.style: Full, waxy, low-acid white with melon, citrus, honey and almond; prone to high alcohol.

places: France (Beaumes de Venise, Rivesaltes, Banyuls, Lunel, St.-Jean-de-Minervois, Alsace)
grapes.style: Grapey, floral family: dry Alsace/Austria whites, fizzy Moscato d'Asti, late-harvest, and fortified raisiny liqueur Muscats.
Clean, crisp apple-pear-almond white, mostly unoaked; one of the most flexible food wines.
Fruity, floral, lightly sweet tank-method sparkler (brut, extra dry, dry); drink young.

places: France (northern Rhône: Hermitage, St.-Joseph, Crozes-Hermitage; Châteauneuf-du-Pape; Savoie; Provence; Languedoc)
U.S.A. (California: Paso Robles, Santa Barbara, Sierra Foothills; Washington)
grapes.style: Roussanne: rich, honeyed, perfumed white of white cherry, herbal tea and pear; silky and age-worthy.

places: France (Bordeaux: Sauternes, Barsac, Graves, Entre-Deux-Mers; Southwest)
Australia (Hunter Valley, Barossa, Adelaide Hills, Margaret River)
grapes.style: Waxy, fig-citrus dry white (toasty with bottle age) and the honeyed heart of Sauternes.

places: Argentina (Salta, La Rioja, Mendoza, Catamarca, San Juan, Rio Negro)
grapes.style: Explosively perfumed, tropical, oily-textured dry white; drink within a year.

places: Italy (Abruzzo, Umbria: Orvieto, Lazio: Frascati, Tuscany: Vin Santo)
grapes.style: Clean, neutral, lemony light white; also the base of Tuscan Vin Santo and of Cognac.
Barrel-aged dried-grape dessert wine, nutty and only moderately sweet.

places: Spain (Basque Country: Getariako, Bizkaiko, Arabako Txakolina)
grapes.style: Light, low-alcohol, lemony, mineral white with a slight spritz; drink very young.
Crisp, herbal, grapefruit-and-pear white like a fruitier Sauvignon Blanc; some oaked or sherry-style versions.

places: Italy (Sardinia: Gallura; Liguria; Tuscany: Bolgheri; Piedmont)
grapes.style: Aromatic, citrus-blossom, green-tea and bitter-almond white; balanced acidity; drink young.
Dense, black-cherry, smoky, tarry red with big tannins and sharp acidity; ages for decades.

places: Australia (Hunter Valley, Mudgee, McLaren Vale, Mornington)
grapes.style: Juicy, high-acid, low-tannin cherry-plum red; light frizzante to oaky modern styles.

places: U.S.A. (Long Island, Virginia, Michigan, Washington, California)
grapes.style: Herbal, leafy, raspberry-and-violet red with balanced acid; also rosé and ice wine.

places: France (Languedoc-Roussillon: Corbières, Minervois, Fitou, Collioure, Banyuls)
grapes.style: High-acid, tannic, peppery black-fruit red best in blends; also fortified Banyuls-style sweet reds.
Smoky, herbal, plum-and-blackberry red with soft tannins; Chile's signature grape.
Best as dry, strawberry-watermelon rosé (Tavel); soft, meaty, peppery red in Lebanon, Morocco, South Africa.
Juicy, grapey, soft, low-acid red with cherry and blueberry; drink young, lightly chilled.

places: France (Beaujolais crus: Morgon, Moulin-à-Vent, Fleurie; Loire: Anjou, Touraine)
grapes.style: Light, low-tannin, bright red-berry red from Nouveau to richer, age-worthy Beaujolais crus.

places: Spain (Priorat, Montsant, Navarra, Rioja, Calatayud, Campo de Borja, Utiel-Requena)
France (Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Gigondas, Vacqueyras, Tavel, Rasteau, Banyuls, Maury, Côtes du Rhône)
grapes.style: Velvety, jammy, low-tannin red-berry red; also great dry rosado and fortified Banyuls.

places: Argentina (Mendoza: Luján de Cuyo, Uco Valley; Salta; San Juan; Patagonia)
grapes.style: Inky, plush plum-blackberry red with soft tannins (Argentina) or firm, austere 'black wine' (Cahors).
Fresh, mineral, raspberry-and-bay-leaf red with moderate alcohol and good acidity.
Dark, peppery, meaty, gamy red with herbs and black fruit; also savory Bandol rosé.

places: Italy (Piedmont: Barolo, Barbaresco, Gattinara, Ghemme, Carema, Langhe)
U.S.A. (California: Paso Robles, Santa Ynez; Washington; Oregon)
grapes.style: Pale but powerful, tannic red of rose, tar, cherry and truffle; age-worthy.

places: U.S.A. (California: Dry Creek, Russian River, Mendocino, Napa, Lodi, Livermore, Amador, Paso Robles)
grapes.style: Inky, peppery, blackberry-and-mocha powerhouse red with big tannin.
Dark-fruited, earthy, smoky, gamy red (Pinot Noir x Cinsaut); modern versions riper and cleaner.

places: France (Southwest: Madiran, Irouléguy, Côtes de St.-Mont, Béarn, Tursan)
grapes.style: Massive, very tannic, blackberry and licorice red; softened by blending and micro-oxygenation; also rosé.

places: Spain (Rioja, Ribera del Duero, Toro, Navarra, Valdepeñas, Penedès, La Mancha, Utiel-Requena)
grapes.style: Cherry, dried-herb (balsamico), tobacco red from elegant Rioja to powerful Toro; aged joven to gran reserva; also rosado.

places: Portugal (Douro, Dão, Alentejo, Tejo, Estremadura, Bairrada)
grapes.style: Inky, floral (violet), black-fruit red with spice; the top grape of port and of Douro and Dão dry reds.
Fortified sweet red; tawny nutty and toffee-like, ruby/vintage plummy and chocolaty.
Pale, high-acid, tannic red of cherry, tomato, olive and spice, like Nebbiolo or Pinot; also rosé and sparkling.

grape_foods.dish: Crab, clams, scallops, shrimp, octopus with pimentón, seafood tapas
grape_foods.why: Lemony acidity lifts the natural sweetness of shellfish; anything from the sea suits it.

grape_foods.dish: Simply cooked fish, crudo, ceviche, sushi, tuna or salmon carpaccio
grape_foods.why: Pure, clean wine matches raw and lightly cooked fish.

grape_foods.dish: Pork, sausage and chicken braises with garlic, olives, greens and potatoes; dry chorizo; country ham
grape_foods.why: Sharp acidity cuts rich stews like caldo gallego; superb with chorizo.

grape_foods.dish: Stir-fried lemon chicken, mild kung pao, duck with ginger, veal braises
grape_foods.why: Clean North Asian flavors and rich white-meat stews suit it.

grape_foods.dish: Fried oysters, fritto of shrimp and calamari, salt cod croquettes, empanadas
grape_foods.why: Zippy, prickly wine refreshes fried and pastry dishes.

grape_foods.dish: Paella, pasta with clams
grape_foods.why: Starchy seafood dishes and lemony herbs flatter it.

grape_foods.dish: Poached or pan-roasted mild white fish, fish and chips, fish with salsa verde
grape_foods.why: Low-impact cooking and green herbs respect its gentle structure.

grape_foods.dish: Pasta with peas and lemon zest; spaghetti puttanesca
grape_foods.why: Low alcohol handles piquant olive-anchovy sauces; light pasta suits it.

grape_foods.dish: Roast chicken with Dijon, quail, Cornish hen
grape_foods.why: Light poultry and mustard show the wine well.

grape_foods.dish: Pork loin with mustard-breadcrumb crust; veal scaloppine with mustard; prosciutto with melon
grape_foods.why: Mustard and mild charcuterie flatter it.

grape_foods.dish: Salt-and-pepper shrimp, simple shellfish, scallop salads
grape_foods.why: Simple shellfish are happy with it.

grape_foods.dish: Antipasti, tapas, mezes (tabbouleh, dolmas, falafel) - vegetarian
grape_foods.why: Versatile with mixed small plates and eastern Mediterranean food.

grape_foods.dish: Oysters, shrimp cocktail, steamed clams, simple seafood with citrus, capers, olives
grape_foods.why: Sharp acidity suits the freshest seafood as in Greek tavernas.

grape_foods.dish: Grilled trout, fish tacos, fish curry, tandoori
grape_foods.why: Bright acid and low alcohol refresh moderately spicy food.

grape_foods.dish: Greek roast lamb with avgolemono
grape_foods.why: Lemony egg sauce makes this classic Greek lamb work with the white.

grape_foods.dish: Simple roast pork or chicken with a green salad
grape_foods.why: White meat served with salad suits its sharpness.

grape_foods.dish: Lobster, scallops, prawns in cream or butter sauce (oaked style)
grape_foods.why: Oak-aged styles behave like Chardonnay.

grape_foods.dish: Dolmas, tzatziki, vegetable pakoras, yogurt-dressed salads - vegetarian
grape_foods.why: Yogurt, dill and tart ingredients match its acidity.

grape_foods.dish: Monkfish, halibut, snapper, poached salmon
grape_foods.why: Dry Chenin works wherever a squeeze of lemon helps.

grape_foods.dish: Oysters, scallops, lobster, coconut shrimp; caviar on corn blinis with sparkling
grape_foods.why: Electric acidity refreshes; sparkling Chenin stands in for Champagne.

grape_foods.dish: Pork or veal scaloppine, ham, smoked pork, sausages, charcuterie; Easter ham
grape_foods.why: Off-dry styles mirror sweetness and balance salt and smoke.

grape_foods.dish: Chicken with Calvados, cream and apples; turkey, quail, duck, goose; barbecue chicken
grape_foods.why: Implied sweetness matches fruit, cream and mild barbecue sauces.

grape_foods.dish: Vindaloo, kimchi, Thai and Kerala coconut curries
grape_foods.why: Off-dry Chenin tames heat and mirrors coconut sweetness.

grape_foods.dish: Terrine of foie gras (sweet Chenin)
grape_foods.why: Sweet Chenin with foie gras is a sublime match.

grape_foods.dish: Apple or pear tart, peach desserts, crème brûlée, honey mousse with pear-quince compote
grape_foods.why: Late-harvest Chenin excels with fruit and custard desserts.

grape_foods.dish: Crab cakes, steamed Dungeness crab with basil aioli, prawns with garlic butter, shrimp
grape_foods.why: Moderately rich texture makes crab an especially good match.

grape_foods.dish: Fish grilled in grape leaves with lemon, swordfish
grape_foods.why: Unoaked Soave suits simple fish with citrus.

grape_foods.dish: Lemon-and-onion roast chicken; poached chicken; chicken with rosemary cream (oaked)
grape_foods.why: Simple poultry suits it; oaked versions take light cream sauces.

grape_foods.dish: Roast loin of pork with lemon-scented risotto
grape_foods.why: Simple white meat with citrus starch is lovely.

grape_foods.dish: Pasta or risotto with pesto or crab; caprese with pesto
grape_foods.why: Pine nut, basil and olive oil have a natural affinity with Soave.

grape_foods.dish: Frittata, leek and goat cheese quiche, eggs - vegetarian
grape_foods.why: One of few wines that handles egg dishes.

grape_foods.dish: Wiener schnitzel with potatoes; ham, sausages, salumi, bratwurst, boudin blanc
grape_foods.why: Classic Austrian partner; acidity balances rich salty meats.

grape_foods.dish: Vietnamese spring rolls, Indian, Thai, Indonesian dishes, noodle stir-fries, tofu
grape_foods.why: Its spicy aromatics mirror Asian herbs and spices; spring rolls are a modern classic.

grape_foods.dish: Sweet-and-sour pork (off-dry GV)
grape_foods.why: Off-dry style handles sweet-sour and sweet-spicy sauces.

grape_foods.dish: Lentil stew with pork and sausage; lima beans and ham; white bean chili
grape_foods.why: Shares the earthy legume character.

grape_foods.dish: Chicken grilled with caraway-cumin North African spices; rabbit with fava and bacon
grape_foods.why: Spice and herb notes link to the wine's pepper.

grape_foods.dish: Asparagus, artichokes, bitter greens, composed salads, strong fish - vegetarian too
grape_foods.why: Handles notoriously wine-hostile vegetables.

grape_foods.dish: Briny oysters (sharp dry GV)
grape_foods.why: Lean, puckery examples love oysters.

grape_foods.dish: Broiled lobster, crayfish étouffée, scallops in brown butter, fish en croûte
grape_foods.why: Rich seafood and butter sauces match its texture.

grape_foods.dish: Brandade of salt cod; hamachi sashimi; macadamia-crusted fish
grape_foods.why: Rich but mild dishes suit it; brandade is a local classic.

grape_foods.dish: Duck; chicken with hazelnuts, cream and sweet spices
grape_foods.why: Nutty notes and richness mirror aged Marsanne.

grape_foods.dish: Shrimp and pea risotto, seafood lasagna, butternut-squash ravioli, pumpkin soup
grape_foods.why: Creamy starches and squash are perfect backdrops.

grape_foods.dish: Veal chops with aligot (veal = Red meat per vocabulary; pork chops also)
grape_foods.why: Rich cheesy potatoes and veal match the wine's texture without overwhelming.

grape_foods.dish: Chicken and cashew stir-fry, roast duck (dry Muscat)
grape_foods.why: Dry Muscat's sharp acidity suits Asian-edged poultry and rich white meat.

grape_foods.dish: Blanquette de veau (dry Alsace Muscat)
grape_foods.why: A favorite pairing of dry Alsace Muscat with creamy veal.

grape_foods.dish: Deep-fried prawns with ginger and garlic; tandoori shrimp (sparkling)
grape_foods.why: Dry Muscat handles mildly sweet Asian sauces; fizz offsets aromatic heat.

grape_foods.dish: Prosciutto and melon; grilled peaches (sparkling Moscato)
grape_foods.why: Salt-sweet picnic food suits fizzy Muscat.

grape_foods.dish: Fresh peaches, nectarines, berries, poached pears, panna cotta, honeyed Greek yogurt (Moscato d'Asti)
grape_foods.why: Light sweet fizz mirrors fresh fruit.

grape_foods.dish: Strawberries and cream, cheesecake, fruit crisps and cobblers (late-harvest)
grape_foods.why: Fresh lively sweetness and cream make strong synergy.

grape_foods.dish: Nut tortes, caramel, butterscotch pudding, bananas with caramel, a little dark chocolate (fortified)
grape_foods.why: Toffee and nut flavors of aged fortified Muscat match.

grape_foods.dish: Oysters, crawfish boil, popcorn shrimp, fried calamari, soft-shell crab salad, crab cakes with aioli
grape_foods.why: Clean, simple flavors and bright acidity suit shellfish and fried food.

grape_foods.dish: Grilled trout with lemon butter, sole amandine, sashimi, steamed fish with ginger, smoked salmon, sardines
grape_foods.why: Hard to find a fish it doesn't suit; works raw to grilled.

grape_foods.dish: Chicken burger, fried chicken, cold roast chicken, chicken brochettes, chicken-pork pâté
grape_foods.why: Loves sandwiches, picnics and homey dishes with a twist.

grape_foods.dish: Cream-based pasta or risotto; macaroni and cheese
grape_foods.why: Rich styles match creamy texture; light ones cut through.

grape_foods.dish: Cold roast pork, picnic sandwiches
grape_foods.why: Classic alfresco wine.

grape_foods.dish: Fried chicken; roast chicken with chutney; Veneto game birds with polenta
grape_foods.why: Salty fried food and lightly sweet sauces love its fruit and bubbles.

grape_foods.dish: Crab and shrimp salads, Hawaiian poke, ceviche, sushi, Thai fish cakes
grape_foods.why: Sweet crab and gentle spice echo its off-dry fruit.

grape_foods.dish: Slow-cooked cured pork belly; salumi; prosciutto-wrapped persimmons
grape_foods.why: Picks up sweetness and cuts salt and fat.

grape_foods.dish: Indian curries, biryani, samosas; Thai coconut curries; mole; empanadas
grape_foods.why: Off-dry fruit handles moderate spice; good beer substitute.

grape_foods.dish: Polenta, pesto, hummus, baba ghanoush, butternut squash stew (vegetarian)
grape_foods.why: Rustic textures and Middle Eastern dips pair nicely.

grape_foods.dish: Fruit and nut desserts, apple galette
grape_foods.why: Works if dessert is no sweeter than the wine.

grape_foods.dish: Lobster, crab cakes, scallops, butter-rich shellfish (Roussanne)
grape_foods.why: Few wines beat Roussanne with crab cakes; texture matches lobster richness.

grape_foods.dish: North African tagines, chicken with apricots and almonds, mild jerk chicken, Thai curry, satay (Roussanne)
grape_foods.why: Silky exotic wine suits aromatic spiced dishes.

grape_foods.dish: Pork marinated in cumin and ginger; honey-glazed ham with cloves (Roussanne)
grape_foods.why: Exotic spices and holiday ham flatter Roussanne.

grape_foods.dish: Holiday goose and turkey (Roussanne)
grape_foods.why: Rich textures of holiday birds suit it.

grape_foods.dish: Butternut squash ravioli with sage and hazelnuts, risotto, polenta, fennel gratin, creamy purées (Roussanne)
grape_foods.why: Rich, buttery starches match its texture.

grape_foods.dish: Veal in rich preparations (Roussanne)
grape_foods.why: Rich white meats suit silky Roussanne.

grape_foods.dish: Shrimp pasta with lemon and cream, scallops with parsnip purée, scallop and pea risotto, fish bisque
grape_foods.why: Waxy texture backs buttery, creamy seafood dishes.

grape_foods.dish: Roast chicken with fig jam; chicken fricassee; honey-mustard or honey-soy glazed poultry (aged Hunter)
grape_foods.why: Plays off the wine's fruit; toasty aged styles like sweet-salt glazes.

grape_foods.dish: Roast pork loin with sautéed apples
grape_foods.why: Fruit in the dish mirrors the wine's fruit.

grape_foods.dish: Veal stew with spring vegetables; veal with mustard cream; sweetbreads
grape_foods.why: White meats and sweetbreads are fabulous with it.

grape_foods.dish: Raw oysters, spring rolls, goat cheese crostini (SSB blends)
grape_foods.why: Zippy SSB acidity highlights fresh seafood and salads.

grape_foods.dish: Spanakopita, pakoras, grilled asparagus, leek-potato soup, vegetable tagine (SSB) - vegetarian
grape_foods.why: Australian SSBs handle green vegetables well.

grape_foods.dish: Foie gras (late-harvest Sémillon/Sauternes)
grape_foods.why: Works if the wine isn't over-sweet; prefer late-harvest to botrytized.

grape_foods.dish: Pear, peach, fig desserts; streusel tarts; crème brûlée, toffee, caramel (Sauternes-style)
grape_foods.why: Stone and tree fruit and caramel echo the honeyed wine.

grape_foods.dish: Scallops, crab, butter-poached lobster, shrimp in lemon-chive cream
grape_foods.why: Oily texture and ripe fruit draw out shellfish sweetness.

grape_foods.dish: Argentine beef-and-raisin empanadas
grape_foods.why: Classic national pairing; sweet-savory filling sings with it.

grape_foods.dish: Sweet-and-sour pork; slow-roasted pork belly
grape_foods.why: Acid-fruit play and caramelized sweetness suit it.

grape_foods.dish: Sauerbraten; short ribs glazed with pomegranate molasses
grape_foods.why: Sweet-sour glazes harmonize with its fruit.

grape_foods.dish: Brazilian moqueca, nut-crusted Caribbean fish, ikan bakar
grape_foods.why: Coconut and tropical flavors match its exuberant fruit.

grape_foods.dish: Hainanese chicken rice, satay, smoked Cornish hen
grape_foods.why: Southeast Asian dishes and gentle smoke-sweetness suit it.

grape_foods.dish: Mild Indian or Southeast Asian curries, mango chutney, plum sauce
grape_foods.why: Fruit and sweet spice echo the wine.

grape_foods.dish: Roast chicken with herbes de Provence and wild rice pilaf
grape_foods.why: Neutral, clean wine won't fight simple weeknight food.

grape_foods.dish: Broiled fish with stir-fried vegetables; trout stuffed with raisins, lemon and pine nuts
grape_foods.why: Brings good simple ingredients into focus; nutty-fruity notes suit it.

grape_foods.dish: Pasta primavera; risotto with cheese and prosciutto (Orvieto or Frascati)
grape_foods.why: Italian rice and pasta dishes pair excellently.

grape_foods.dish: Crab and rice pilaf with lemon and almonds
grape_foods.why: Toasty, nutty, lemony dish lifts the straightforward wine.

grape_foods.dish: Squid, fried calamari, crab, oysters, steamed clams and mussels
grape_foods.why: Acidity and spritz lift seafood and tame saltiness.

grape_foods.dish: Salt cod (bacalao), crunchy fried fish
grape_foods.why: Salt cod and Txakoli are the classic Basque match.

grape_foods.dish: Dry chorizo, pintxos/tapas, bocadillos
grape_foods.why: Tapas and Txakoli are a match made in heaven.

grape_foods.dish: Chicken wings, grilled chicken, satays, pizza (anything you'd drink with pilsner)
grape_foods.why: Light, bubbly, refreshing like lager.

grape_foods.dish: Gyoza, ginger-steamed fish, spring rolls, pad Thai, Chinese takeout
grape_foods.why: Low alcohol and spritz suit Asian dishes.

grape_foods.dish: Ceviche, smoked trout salad with grapefruit, grilled swordfish with caper butter, seared tuna with lemon pesto
grape_foods.why: Vivid acidity highlights clean fish without masking it.

grape_foods.dish: Shrimp tartine with pesto, tuna poke, crawfish boil
grape_foods.why: Shrimp bring out its natural sweetness; nuts and herbs echo the wine.

grape_foods.dish: Pork or veal with citrus, capers, garlic, olives, ginger
grape_foods.why: Sharp seasonings spike its flavors.

grape_foods.dish: Chicken grilled with rosemary or lemon thyme; chicken pasta with sun-dried tomato and cream
grape_foods.why: Fresh herbs and pesto match its herbal side.

grape_foods.dish: Lamb brochette in herb marinade
grape_foods.why: Herbs downplay meatiness so the white works.

grape_foods.dish: Green vegetable soups, minestrone, watercress, sorrel, spinach, Greek salad, guacamole - vegetarian
grape_foods.why: Handles bitter greens and vinaigrettes others can't.

grape_foods.dish: Spicy-hot dishes (fruity, slightly sweet examples best)
grape_foods.why: Bright acid and low alcohol refresh the palate.

grape_foods.dish: Salmon carpaccio, sashimi, tuna tartare, grilled whole fish with potatoes, pan-roasted halibut
grape_foods.why: One of the best wines for raw and simply cooked fish.

grape_foods.dish: Scallop brochettes, shrimp risotto, fried anchovies, panko shrimp, fritto misto
grape_foods.why: Moderate alcohol and zest handle a pop of salt and fried batter.

grape_foods.dish: Fettuccine with shrimp and garlic, penne with squid or clams and peas
grape_foods.why: Pasta is a blank canvas that lets it star.

grape_foods.dish: Mild salumi with green olives; pork and veal (richer Sardinian/Corsican styles)
grape_foods.why: Simple charcuterie and white meats work with richer versions.

grape_foods.dish: Chicken with coconut rice, mild coconut curry, Asian chicken salad, shrimp Caesar
grape_foods.why: Gentle coconut and main-course salads suit it.

grape_foods.dish: Osso buco, oxtails, braised short ribs, daubes, large steaks, offal
grape_foods.why: Gelatin-rich braises and fat tame its massive tannins.

grape_foods.dish: Braised lamb shanks, grilled chops
grape_foods.why: Classic rustic match for almost any Aglianico.

grape_foods.dish: Sausage and bean stews, feijoada, sausages with lentils; pork and veal with older wines
grape_foods.why: Hearty meat-and-bean dishes call for young Aglianico.

grape_foods.dish: Lasagna, baked ziti, pasta with meat ragù, mushroom and Parma ham risotto
grape_foods.why: Thick rich pastas match its weight; tomato in a meaty sauce brings out fruit.

grape_foods.dish: Rich duck, goose, squab
grape_foods.why: Only robust birds stand up to it.

grape_foods.dish: Pizza, pasta with tomato sauce, mushroom risotto
grape_foods.why: High acidity is the quintessential match for red sauces; few wines better with pizza.

grape_foods.dish: Salumi, prosciutto, mortadella, pâté, terrines; char siu
grape_foods.why: Acidity cuts rich cured pork, a northern Italian tradition.

grape_foods.dish: Burgers, meat loaf, burritos, veal chops with mushrooms, steak au poivre, osso buco, shaking beef
grape_foods.why: Comfort food magnet; oaky modern styles handle rich meats.

grape_foods.dish: Simple roast lamb, lamb stew
grape_foods.why: Full Barbera holds its own with lamb.

grape_foods.dish: Grilled tuna, swordfish, halibut with tomato vinaigrette or puttanesca
grape_foods.why: Great red for meaty fish thanks to acid and low tannin.

grape_foods.dish: Chicken liver pâté crostini, tandoori chicken
grape_foods.why: Acid cuts liver richness; red fruit suits meatiness.

grape_foods.dish: Veal saltimbocca, herbed meat stews
grape_foods.why: Sage, rosemary and thyme echo its herbal character.

grape_foods.dish: Rosemary-marinated pork brochettes; pasta with pancetta, sausage or prosciutto
grape_foods.why: Herbs and cured pork bridge to the wine.

grape_foods.dish: Seared tuna with sautéed spinach (Loire style)
grape_foods.why: Cooked meaty tuna and greens suit leaner Cab Franc.

principles.rule: Wine acidity is the most important pairing factor; tart wines cut rich, salty, oily, fried or mildly spicy dishes like a squeeze of lemon.
With sharp foods (vinaigrette salads, capers, tomatoes, leeks) the wine must be at least as tart as the dish or it tastes thin.
High-acid whites and sparkling wines handle salty food better than most reds; tannin makes salt seem stronger.
Low-acid whites such as Trebbiano or Marsanne are harder to pair; give them mild dishes with a squeeze of citrus.
Off-dry wines tame moderate chili heat and echo slightly sweet fruit sauces, chutneys and salsas.
Sweet wine against salty food (Sauternes with Roquefort, port with Stilton) works but needs testing.
A dessert wine must be at least as sweet as the dessert; dry bubbly with sugary frosting tastes sour.
Grilled, charred or naturally bitter foods flatter tannic reds; fat and protein in rare red meat soften tannin.
Hard aged cheeses can make tannic reds taste metallic, and stinky soft cheeses bring out ammonia notes in big reds.
Tannic reds with oily fish give a metallic taste; low-tannin reds like Gamay manage fish far better.
Food amplifies oak; match oaky wines with grilled, smoked, blackened or caramelized dishes, and prefer unoaked wines for flexibility.
Match the weight of wine and dish: medium reds (Barbera, Pinotage) with roast chicken, rich Aglianico with lasagna.
Salt and chili heat make high-alcohol wines taste hotter; keep powerful wines away from spicy food.
Cured meats like prosciutto or bacon can steer fish, poultry or pork dishes toward light reds and rosés.
Delicate herbs suit Assyrtiko and Arneis; pungent herbs like rosemary and basil suit Verdejo, Carmenère and Cabernet Franc.
Green olives push a dish toward Vermentino, Albariño or Verdejo; black olives toward Carmenère, Cinsaut or Mencía.
Dark mushrooms make most dishes red-friendly; light creamy mushrooms favor textured whites like Roussanne and Marsanne.
Serving fish on green lentils or beans lets it pair with red wine.
The sauce usually dictates the wine; rich buttery or creamy sauces want textured wines like Roussanne, Torrontés or Grenache.
Side dishes and condiments can matter more than the main ingredient when choosing wine.
Use juicy fruity reds (Rioja joven, Beaujolais, Dolcetto) for sangria; peaches macerated in good Moscato d'Asti.
With tart food avoid most reds; only sharp reds like Barbera, Xinomavro or Gamay cope, and rosé or sparkling are good options.
Slightly sweet dishes need a slightly sweet wine such as Chenin Blanc, Prosecco or Muscat.
Salty dishes want low-to-moderate alcohol wines, perhaps with a touch of sweetness, and no heavy oak or tannin.
For spicy dishes choose young, low-alcohol, unoaked, off-dry whites or rosés, or sparkling; very fiery food calls for beer.
Aged reds suit simple rare meats; aged whites suit nutty, dried-fruit or sherry flavors plus a touch of citrus.
Very hot-temperature dishes exaggerate alcohol; let them cool or serve chilled wine.
Assyrtiko often feels too intense alone; serve it with at least olives or nuts.
Treat Chenin Blanc like Riesling: pick dry, off-dry, sparkling or sweet to suit the dish, never mismatched.
Grüner Veltliner craves food; even sushi or olives beat drinking it alone.
Too much salt in a dish (e.g. salty clams) spikes a rich white's alcohol and dulls its fruit.
Light spritzy whites like Txakoli can stand in for pilsner beer with bar snacks, wings and pizza.
Treat sherry-style whites like dry sherry: olives, nuts, semi-hard cheese, seafood, brothy soups.
Pure tomato sauce can strip big reds; tomato within a meaty sauce brings out their fruit.
In Piedmont, drink Barbera with antipasti and pasta, then move to Barolo or Barbaresco for the main course.
If the wine is oaky, play to the oak with grilling, char and smoky flavors.
Dry rosé is a serious food wine: almost any fish or shellfish, Chinese family meals, paella and gumbo.
Classic red-wine-with-fish matches: salmon with Dolcetto or Pinot Noir, tuna with Merlot; a red wine sauce links them.
Light fruity reds (Dolcetto, Gamay, Barbera) improve with a light chill for picnics and spicy food.
Malbec breaks the rule that big reds dislike strong cheese: it handles Roquefort and Gorgonzola.
Wines with herbal notes shine when herbs go on the grill or into marinades and sauces.
Pomegranate molasses gives tang without hurting red wine the way vinegar does.
Older reds need simple, juicy food: rare meat, or a little prune purée or tomato paste in the sauce.
Salt exaggerates alcohol and hard tannin; with tannic reds season lightly and add more at the end.
Wine age game: the rarer the meat, the older the wine; serve stews and long-cooked cuts with young wines.
Tempranillo can carry a whole meal: rosado to start, young red with the first course, a fuller one with the main.
For vegetarian dishes reach for high-acid reds: Cabernet Franc, Carmenère and Xinomavro.
Reducing the same wine to a glaze, rather than marinating in it, keeps meat texture and links dish to wine.
